title: Two men were walking away from Jerusalem.
paragraphs: Two men were walking away from Jerusalem.

Their hopes had collapsed.
Everything they believed about the future seemed broken.

They had followed Jesus.
They had trusted Him.
They believed He was the One who would change everything.

But now…
He was gone.
So they walked the long road to Emmaus, replaying the pain, the confusion, the disappointment.
And then something unexpected happened.
A stranger joined them on the road.

He walked beside them.
He listened to them.
He asked questions.
For miles, they talked.

They shared their heartbreak.
They explained the story of Jesus.
They wondered why everything had fallen apart.
And the stranger gently began explaining the Scriptures to them.
What they didn’t realize was the most incredible part of the story.
The stranger was Jesus Himself.
He had been walking with them the entire time.
They just didn’t recognize Him yet.
Sometimes life feels exactly like that road.

You thought things would work out.
You expected a different ending.
You believed God was leading you somewhere… and then everything suddenly changed.
In those moments it can feel like you’re walking alone.
But the truth is something deeper.
God often walks with us before we realize He’s there.

In the confusion.
In the disappointment.
In the unanswered questions.
He is closer than we think.
And sometimes the biggest miracle isn’t that God shows up.
It’s discovering that He was with you the whole journey.
Maybe you’re on a road like that right now.
A road where things don’t make sense yet.
But the Emmaus story reminds us of something powerful:

Just because you don’t recognize His presence…
doesn’t mean He isn’t walking beside you.
And one day, like those travelers, the moment will come when you look back and realize:
He was there the entire time.
